_about: Work that could be removed, merged or done more cheaply. scripts/cpu_report.py prices each from the capture: cost = on-CPU samples with a frame matching 'match' anywhere in the stack (once a sample); 'gain' is the share of that cost the fix is expected to remove, always an estimate; 'evidence' names a measurement that supports the estimate, if there is one. 'game_own' rows are the game's own large costs, listed for scale. Keys are frame keys as the report prints them.

candidates.title: The scan for written pages at every submission
candidates.what: Reads and clears the lifted code's write marks over every GPU-visible range, 32 pages at a time, at every submission; its cost follows the pools' size, not what was written.
candidates.fix: A summary level over the marks (one bit for a few hundred pages, set where the mark is set) so clean spans cost nothing.
candidates.risk: medium: a missed page is stale data on the GPU; needs the capture tests and Codex's content check

candidates.title: Each recorded command buffer copied when its recording ends
candidates.what: nvnCommandBufferEndRecording copies the recorded commands into a pooled block that becomes the handle.
candidates.fix: Hand the recorded segment over as the handle and give the command buffer a fresh segment.
candidates.risk: medium: recording memory ownership; the renderer's correctness gate

candidates.title: A recording copied again when it is called, under a shared lock
candidates.what: nvnCommandBufferCallCommands inlines the called recording by copying it and checks the handle under a shared lock.
candidates.fix: Reference the called recording instead of copying it; check the handle without the lock.
candidates.risk: medium: a called recording freed while referenced

candidates.title: The submitting thread moved onto the reserved core and back for every replay
candidates.what: ReplayPin sets the submitting thread's affinity to the core reserved for the replay before each submission's replay and restores the old mask after it (two SetThreadAffinityMask calls a submission); game threads' own mask leaves that core out.
candidates.fix: Keep the thread on the reserved core across back-to-back submissions and restore the mask once, or skip the pair when the replay is too short to gain from the core.
candidates.risk: medium: the game thread runs on the reserved core longer; the replay's own core use changes
candidates.evidence: stacks: about two thirds of the calls are on the Presentation Thread and a third on the main thread; each moves to the reserved core and back for every replay

candidates.title: Idle job workers' 20 us sleeps answered by a busy loop
candidates.what: The game's idle job workers sleep 20 us at a time, very often; under 1 ms the host yields in a loop until the time, keeping a processor busy.
candidates.fix: The short-sleep timer on PCs with few logical processors (PR 2263, measured with its own code: fps up 9.2 % on 4 logical processors); a cheaper wait elsewhere.
candidates.risk: low to medium: a longer sleep delays a job's start
candidates.evidence: measured with PR 2263's own code: on 4 logical processors fps +9.2 % (47.0 to 51.3) and no frame over 250 ms (2 of 4 runs had one before); on 6, CPU a frame -9 % at the same fps. On 16 the timer for every short sleep saved 5 to 13 % of the process's CPU at the same fps and is not proposed there (3 of 32 runs with a 250 ms frame against 0 of 38)

candidates.title: The 20 us spin before an event or queue wait sleeps
candidates.what: Each light-event or queue wait spins up to 20 us before sleeping; three of four waits end inside the spin.
candidates.fix: A 5 us spin (HOS_SPIN_US=5), or an adaptive one.
candidates.risk: low: wake latency; measured fps unchanged
candidates.evidence: measured: process CPU -3 % on 16 threads at the same fps

candidates.title: Every mutex lock and unlock through the host's object table
candidates.what: Each lock and unlock finds the host object of the guest mutex.
candidates.fix: An uncontended fast path in the guest's own mutex memory, as the SDK does it.
candidates.risk: high: guest-visible layout, condition-variable hand-off, virtual cores

candidates.title: Exact floating-point helpers in vector code
candidates.what: Bit-exact ARM floating-point results for operations x86 rounds differently; the game's vector code needs them often.
candidates.fix: More per-helper fast paths that stay bit-exact.
candidates.risk: high: one wrong bit changes game behaviour; needs exhaustive stubs

candidates.title: The GPU-visible ranges re-sorted at every submission while mappings change
candidates.what: qsort of the GPU-visible ranges at each submission when a mapping changed since the last one (often, while streaming).
candidates.fix: Keep the list sorted on insert and removal.

candidates.title: getenv on hot paths
candidates.what: Environment switches read with getenv at every present (menu_vsync), every dispatch (taau_stand_in) and every file open; only the getenv calls are counted.
candidates.fix: Read each switch once into a static.

candidates.title: The C runtime's stat opens the volume on every call
candidates.what: stat on the loading threads asks for the drive type each time, which opens the volume.
candidates.fix: A stat that does not ask for the drive type (GetFileAttributesEx).

candidates.title: GetThreadPriority under a shared lock
candidates.what: Called many times a frame from the game's worker loops.
candidates.fix: Read the priority without the lock.

candidates.title: SignalConditionVariable with nobody waiting
candidates.what: Signals take a lock pair and make a wake call even when nobody waits.
candidates.fix: Return early when the waiter count is 0, with the ordering argument written down.
candidates.risk: low to medium: a missed wake is a hang

candidates.title: Trivial OS calls made through the full call path
candidates.fix: Answer them in the lifted code with a field read.
